doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cal Massey, Coltrane and the Jazztet
title: Early playing with Coltrane and 'The Believer'
summary: Tyner discusses rehearsing with Coltrane at his Philadelphia house, Coltrane recording 'The Believer', and Benny Golson's and Coltrane's school days.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well let’s go back before we get into your tenure with John and or with the Jazztet and talk about your early encounter with John. I believe he recorded one of your pieces, “The Believer”, is that correct?
He recorded that in the late fifties before you joined the band.

Something like that. Your stats are probably better than mine (laughs). Well I wrote a book so it’s all in there, it’s not implanted deep in my psyche but it’s there you know . . . somewhere (laughs).
So did you exchange musical ideas, did you actually play with him before you joined the group?
Yeah, I was in Cal’s band and Cal was a good friend of John’s.
But you did play with him too, they used to have rehearsals at his house on 33rd Street and Fairmount, that’s where John lived, [across from] Fairmount Park.
And she’s from North Philly and her sister sang with that band so . . .
And when we interviewed Benny Golson he talked about how in High School, John and he would get together and practice.
What High School did Benny go to?
Ah, you got me, I’m sorry, I don’t remember.
Lee Morgan went to Bartrum, he [Tyner] went to West Philly, I was in North Philly so I went to a totally different school, but I don’t remember.
It’s hard to remember a lot of these things.
